prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a land or people named in the book of Daniel, from Babylon to Grecia
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a land, city or people named in the book of Daniel (Babylon, Shushan by the river Ulai, Media and Persia, Grecia, Egypt, the Libyans and the people of Cush, the Nile land south of Egypt, Edom, Moab and Ammon, the ships of Chittim, and the glorious land)
prompts.note: Bible Ethiopia (Cush) lay mostly in today's Sudan, reaching into southern Egypt, so Sudan counts for Daniel 11:43.
prompts.summary: Daniel was taken captive to Babylon, served under Babylonian and Persian kings, and saw visions at Shushan. His visions trace Media and Persia, Grecia, and the long struggle of the kings of the north and south, which touches Egypt, Libya, Ethiopia, Edom, Moab, Ammon and the ships of Chittim (Dan 1-11).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Daniel was carried to Babylon in the land of Shinar (Dan 1:1-2).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: The king of the south of Daniel 11 rules Egypt (Dan 11:8, 42).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Daniel saw his vision at Shushan by the river of Ulai, and the ram stood for the kings of Media and Persia (Dan 8:2, 20).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Daniel prayed toward Jerusalem, and the king of the north enters the glorious land (Dan 6:10; 11:41).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: The rough goat is the king of Grecia (Dan 8:21).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Edom, Moab and the chief of the children of Ammon escape out of his hand (Dan 11:41).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: The Libyans shall be at his steps (Dan 11:43).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The king of the north stands in the glorious land and plants his palace in the glorious holy mountain; that land includes the hill country now in the West Bank (Dan 11:16, 41, 45).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: The ships of Chittim come against the king of the north (Dan 11:30); Chittim is Cyprus.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: The Ethiopians shall be at his steps (Dan 11:43); Bible Ethiopia (Cush) was the Nile land south of Egypt.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place, city or river named in the book of Revelation
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place, city or river named in the book of Revelation
prompts.note: The Euphrates also rises in Turkey, which is already accepted.
prompts.summary: John wrote Revelation on Patmos, a Greek island, to seven churches in western Turkey. The book names the great river Euphrates, which flows through Turkey, Syria and Iraq, and Armageddon, the mount of Megiddo in Israel. It also calls the wicked city spiritually Sodom and Egypt.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: The seven churches, from Ephesus to Laodicea, were in the province of Asia in western Turkey (Revelation 1:11).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: John received the revelation on the isle of Patmos (Revelation 1:9).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Armageddon is Har Megiddo, the mount of Megiddo in northern Israel (Revelation 16:16; Bible Dictionary).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The Euphrates and the site of Babylon are in Iraq (Revelation 9:14; 16:12; 14:8).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: The great river Euphrates flows across Syria (Revelation 9:14; 16:12).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: The great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt (Revelation 11:8).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country in the Americas with a Pacific coastline and at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A country in the Americas with a Pacific Ocean coastline and at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology (dedicated, under construction, announced), read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Thirteen Pacific-coast countries of the Americas have a dedicated temple, from Canada and the United States down through Mexico, Central America, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Chile. Honduras is the trick answer: its short Pacific shore on the Gulf of Fonseca is easy to forget. Belize and the Caribbean islands have no Pacific coast.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Fourteen dedicated temples.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Pacific coast from California to Alaska; most temples of any country.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Vancouver British Columbia Temple 2010 on the Pacific.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Santiago, Concepción, Antofagasta.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Lima and three more.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Pacific and Caribbean coasts; Bogotá and Barranquilla.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Guayaquil 1999 and Quito 2022.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Guatemala City, Quetzaltenango, Cobán, Miraflores.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: San José Costa Rica Temple 2000.

answers.name: Nicaragua
answers.fact: Managua Nicaragua Temple October 2026.

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: Panama City Panama Temple 2008.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: San Salvador El Salvador Temple 2011.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: Honduras touches the Pacific at the Gulf of Fonseca; Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula temples.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory with a Church stake but fewer than 5,000 members as of October 2026.
prompts.text_original: A country or territory that has at least one stake even though the Church counts fewer than 5,000 members there (as of October 2026, year-end 2025 figures).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (figures of 31 Dec 2025), read 4 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: A stake normally needs a few thousand members, so countries with stakes but under 5,000 members are rare. They include Austria, Ireland, Denmark, Norway, Singapore, Albania, the Czech Republic, Cameroon, Trinidad and Tobago, Guam, New Caledonia and the United Arab Emirates. Bahrain is the extreme case: its stake gathers members from across the Gulf, so the country itself counts only 231.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: 2 stakes; 4,753 members.

answers.name: Ireland
answers.fact: 1 stake; 4,923 members.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: 2 stakes; 4,426 members.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: 2 stakes; 4,547 members.

answers.name: Singapore
answers.fact: 1 stake; 3,262 members.

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: 1 stake; 3,285 members.

answers.name: Cameroon
answers.fact: 1 stake; 3,673 members.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: 1 stake; 2,628 members.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: 1 stake; 2,768 members.

answers.name: Trinidad and Tobago
answers.fact: 1 stake; 3,458 members.

answers.name: United Arab Emirates
answers.fact: 1 stake; 2,002 members.

answers.name: Bahrain
answers.fact: 1 stake; 231 members, the smallest membership with a stake.

answers.name: New Caledonia
answers.fact: 1 stake; 2,585 members.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Pacific island country or territory dedicated for the preaching of the gospel between 1947 and 1998.
prompts.text_original: A Pacific island country or territory dedicated for the preaching of the gospel between 1947 and 1998.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Cook Islands, Guam, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, French Polynesia, Fiji; RSC (New Caledonia); Newsroom (Solomon Islands); Ensign Nov 1996 (Nauru, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna)
prompts.summary: Dedicatory prayers followed the Church across the Pacific long after the first Polynesian missions: the Cook Islands in 1947, Guam in 1955, New Caledonia in 1968, Kiribati in 1975, Papua New Guinea in 1983, the Solomon Islands in 1987, French Polynesia (rededicated) in 1994, six island groups by L. Tom Perry in 1996, and Fiji in 1998. Tonga, Samoa and New Zealand had been mission fields since the 1800s.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: L. Tom Perry offered the dedicatory prayer for Fiji in Suva on June 17, 1998.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: L. Tom Perry dedicated Papua New Guinea in Port Moresby on April 14, 1983.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: Russell M. Nelson rededicated French Polynesia on May 8, 1994, for the 150th anniversary of the Church there.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: Joseph Fielding Smith offered a dedicatory prayer on Guam on August 25, 1955.

answers.name: Kiribati
answers.fact: Dedicated by mission president Kenneth M. Palmer on October 20, 1975 and rededicated by L. Tom Perry in 1996.

answers.name: Cook Islands
answers.fact: Matthew Cowley dedicated the Cook Islands for the preaching of the gospel on July 1, 1947.

answers.name: New Caledonia
answers.fact: Thomas S. Monson dedicated New Caledonia from Mount Coffyn above Noumea on May 2, 1968.

answers.name: Nauru
answers.fact: L. Tom Perry dedicated Nauru for the preaching of the gospel on August 10, 1996.

answers.name: Solomon Islands
answers.fact: James E. Faust dedicated the Solomon Islands for the preaching of the gospel on March 10, 1987.

answers.name: Tuvalu
answers.fact: L. Tom Perry dedicated Tuvalu for the preaching of the gospel on August 10, 1996.

answers.name: Vanuatu
answers.fact: L. Tom Perry dedicated Vanuatu, with Kiribati, Nauru, Tuvalu, Tokelau and Wallis and Futuna, on August 10, 1996.

answers.name: Wallis and Futuna
answers.fact: L. Tom Perry dedicated Wallis and Futuna for the preaching of the gospel on August 10, 1996.
